Give your blank wall a chance before deciding it needs a major renovation.

This wall started completely blank, but layering just a few intentional pieces—a console table, oversized mirror, lighting and simple decor—gave it purpose and turned it into one of my favorite little moments in the house.

That’s something I’ve learned over and over while designing my own home: sometimes the room isn’t missing more. It’s just missing the right pieces, scale, and layers.

If you have an empty wall, awkward entryway, unused living room wall, or blank hallway, try creating a focal point instead of filling it randomly. Start with one substantial furniture piece, add something with height above it, then layer in a few accessories for warmth and personality.

A blank wall can become a statement without becoming cluttered.

1. Size & Proportion
Think about the wall where it will live. The right piece should feel balanced with the size and scale of the wall, not lost in the space or overwhelming it.

2. Style & Color
Choose something that feels like you. Your furniture should complement your existing décor while also reflecting your personality and the way you want your home to feel.

3. Storage & Organization
We can all use a little extra storage! 😉 
If you’re going to bring a beautiful piece into your home, why not choose one that also helps keep things organized?

4. Practicality
This is where my three-piece credenza is GOLDEN. 🤎 
I love that I can use all three pieces together as one grand statement on a massive wall, but I can also separate them and use them in different rooms if my needs change.

Beautiful + functional + versatile = a piece you’ll love for years.

The secret to beautiful fall decor? Less is more.

You don’t need pumpkins on every surface, fall signs in every corner, or an entirely new collection of seasonal decorations to make your home feel like autumn.

Sometimes all it takes is a few thoughtfully chosen pieces, warmer textures, soft candlelight, natural elements, and subtle touches of fall color.

As a Charlotte interior designer, I believe seasonal decorating should complement your home’s existing design, not compete with it.

My favorite way to decorate for fall is to create an atmosphere rather than a theme. A home that feels warm, cozy, collected, and inviting without looking overly decorated.

Whether I’m styling my own home or designing for clients in Charlotte, Waxhaw, and Weddington, I always come back to the same principle: beautiful design is about knowing what to add and what to leave out.

Are you a minimalist fall decorator, or do you love going all out?
